home.control.s:
Set hours and minutes to run, then switch the device on. A countdown replaces the boxes while it runs;

Below the switch is the next enabled schedule that will start. In case of cyclic schedule the next cycle that will start will be shown.

home.telemetry.s:
Voltage, current, power, this session's energy and cumulative energy, updated live from the device.
Power and energy are not measured on 3-phase installations.

home.alerts.s: Fault and information messages such as dry run, overload, low or high voltage, and float switch state.

home.logs.s: The latest device events with date and time. Use "More" to open the full log with filters.

schedule.details.s:
Schedule Type: Daily runs every day; Weekly runs only on the days ticked under Run Every.

Duration based schedules will run only for the duration and only between the selected timings. Enable Restart after power resumption in protection settings to complete duration even after a power-cut.

Timings: start and end time of the run. They cannot be the same, and an end time earlier than the start is treated as running past midnight.

The toggle at the top enables or disables this schedule without deleting it; the bin removes it for good.

schedule.cyclic.s: Repeats an on/off cycle between the start and end time instead of running continuously.

power.dryrunCurrent.s:
The device stops if current stays below this value for 4 to 7 seconds.
Example: a pump running with no water draws about 20% less than its normal current.

power.dryrunRestart.s: Tick this to let the device try again after a dryrun fault, and set the retry time below.

power.dryrunRetry.s: Delay in minutes before the device retries after a dryrun fault.

power.protectionOnly.s: Choose Yes if this unit sits before a master switch and only protects the load instead of controlling it.

power.thresholdCurrent.s: For a protection-only device, dryrun detection starts only once current has reached this value.

power.overcurrent.s:
The device stops if current stays above this value for 4 to 7 seconds.
Example: a seized shaft or damaged winding draws about 20% more than the normal current.

power.overcurrentRestart.s: Tick this to let the device try again after an overload fault, and set the retry time below.

power.overcurrentRetry.s: Delay in minutes before the device retries after an overload fault.

power.lowVoltage.s:
The device will not start, and stops while running, if voltage stays below this value for more than 7 seconds.
Running a motor on low voltage makes it draw more current and heat up.

power.lowVoltageRestart.s:
Tick this to let the device try again after a low voltage fault.
On 3-phase units this setting also covers phase failure and phase sequence reversal.

power.lowVoltageRetry.s:
Delay in minutes before the device retries after a low voltage fault.
Retries happen only within the scheduled time; if the retry falls after it, the device stays off.

power.highVoltage.s:
The device stops if voltage goes above this value.
Sustained high voltage damages motor insulation and capacitors over time.

power.highVoltageRestart.s: Tick this to let the device try again after a high voltage fault.

power.highVoltageRetry.s:
Delay in minutes before the device retries after a high voltage fault.
Retries happen only within the scheduled time; if the retry falls after it, the device stays off.

power.powerResumeRestart.s: Tick this to let the device start again by itself once mains power comes back during a run or a schedule.

power.restartDelay.s:
Minutes to wait before restarting after power resumes.
The delay protects the load from the voltage spikes that often follow a power cut.

power.maxRunDuration.s: Longest the device may run continuously before it must take a break. Valid range is 1 to 1440 minutes.

power.breakTime.s: How long the device stays off after reaching the maximum run duration. Valid range is 1 to 1440 minutes.

settings.deviceTime.s:
The device's own clock, synchronised every time you open this page.
When the SuperSmart is on Wi-Fi the time syncs automatically. If the battery is down, a warning will appear here

settings.wifi.s:
Connect the device to your local Wi-Fi so you can reach this portal from anywhere on that network.
If the saved network is unavailable the device falls back to its own access point.
Remove Wi-Fi forgets the saved network and puts the device back into access point mode - connect to the device's own _AP network to reach this portal again.

settings.wifiIp.s:
Optional. Set a preferred IP so the portal is always at the same address; reserve it in your router too.
Subnet mask and DNS are needed only if your network differs from the defaults.

settings.deviceName.s:
A name of 4 to 20 characters, for example Sump-motor. The device restarts after a name change.
The portal is then also reachable at http://name.local

settings.devicePin.s: A 4-digit PIN that protects access to this portal.

settings.apPassword.s:
Password for the device's own Wi-Fi network, named after the device with _AP added.
Set one so nobody nearby can connect to the device.

settings.logs.s: Clear all stored operation logs, or reset the cumulative energy counter back to zero.

settings.restart.s:
Restart reboots the device for troubleshooting.
Clear Fault Conditions resumes operation once a dryrun, overload or voltage fault has been fixed, without waiting for the retry delay.

settings.cloud.s: Enter your email address to register this device with the EVIQtech cloud. You will receive a link to set your password.

settings.cloudStatus.s: Shows the cloud connection state. If the device stays disconnected, check your Wi-Fi and that your router allows outgoing port 1883.

settings.firmware.s: Install a newer firmware file on the device. Do not switch off power while an update is running.

settings.floatSwitch.s:
Tank Full: connect the float switch NO contacts, which close when the tank is full.
Flow or Tank Full/Empty: NO contacts of a flow paddle switch detect flow, or NC float contacts start and stop the pump by tank level.

settings.floatFlowDelay.s: Seconds to wait after flow starts or stops before the relay is switched. Valid range is 0 to 300 seconds.

settings.masterRemote.s:
Master accepts on/off signals from a remote SuperSmart; Remote sends them to a master.
For local Wi-Fi control both units must be on the same network and you must give the master's URL and PIN.

firstuse.device.s:
Give the device a name and a 4-digit PIN so the portal can be identified and protected.
The default name works, but change it if another SuperSmart is nearby, or name it after the job - Sump-motor, Geiser-2.

firstuse.wifi.s:
Optional. Join the device to your WiFi so the portal is reachable from anywhere on that network.
Skip it for now and set it later under Settings; the device keeps its own access point either way.

login.pin.s:
The 4-digit PIN set during setup.
If it has been forgotten, factory reset the device by holding the second, third and stop buttons together for 20 seconds until the blue LED lights. A reset clears all settings.

techsetup.circuit.s:
How the device is wired: shunt or CT current sensing, LED-pin type, single or 3-phase motor, 5V DC tapping, Ethernet, and leak detection.
These match the hardware build and should not be changed on a working unit.

techsetup.inrush.s:
Added on top of the built-in 7-second settle time before overload protection starts.
Useful for motors with a long inrush or a delayed self-starter.

techsetup.timing.s:
Sets the run durations offered by the physical buttons on the device.
Cloud server access must be configured before any data is sent.

cert.upload.s:
Replaces the built-in root CA used for the secure cloud connection.
Upload a PEM file or paste its text. Only needed when your network inspects TLS traffic.

mqtt.sync.s:
Choose Yes to send telemetry and logs to the cloud.
With No the device runs entirely on its own and keeps data locally.

mqtt.access.s:
The access token that identifies this device to the cloud server.
It must be set before any data can be sent.
